messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: SEV=page FIRING -> service=postgres-reddb-prod connections (trigger: pg_connections > 350)

pagerduty-bot: page  --> https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD12345  assigned to: oncall@redwood  :rotating_light:

alex: acked on PD, hopping in. seeing lots of active conns in the pg dashboard (conn_count ~ 420, wait avg 230ms).

maya: +1, confirmed. slow queries heatmap shows spike from app-service-worker:v3 around 17:11 UTC.

alex: running quick check on primary: `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;` returns 418. a bunch are idle in transaction from app-worker.

maya: logs show `BEGIN` started but not commit for many requests; looks like retry loop holding connections. suspect recent deploy?

sam: who deployed last hour? @product? :thinking:

alex: last deploy was app-worker v3.4.1 at 17:02 UTC (deploy-bot).

maya: mitigation plan: 1) reduce app-worker concurrency to limit new connections 2) enable fallback read from replica for non-write paths 3) prepare to kill offending pods if needed.

alex: applying immediate throttling — scaling down replicas of app-worker from 12 -> 4 (kubectl scale).

maya: patch applied: set env WORKER_CONCURRENCY=8 via rollout pause. rolling update to reduce concurrency.

pagerduty-bot: PD note: incident acknowledged by alex at 17:13 UTC. Escalation timer paused.

alex: observed conn_count drop to ~280 after scale-down + patch. latency improved. still seeing ~30 stuck idle-in-transaction.

maya: I'm going to identify offending queries: `select pid, state, query, query_start from pg_stat_activity where state!='idle' order by query_start desc limit 20;` shows long-running `INSERT INTO events ...` from worker job id 42.

sam: can we safely restart just the 3 worker pods showing bad pids?

alex: yes planning a rolling restart of those pods in the worker ASG. doing `kubectl delete pod worker-abc-123` for the three.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: restart jobs triggered by oncall.

maya: after restarts, stuck connections cleared. conn_count back to ~120. 95th p99 latencies back to normal.

alex: customer impact: short tail of increased error rate for real-time ingestion customers between 17:07-17:18 UTC. Estimated affected requests ~ 0.6% of traffic. No long-running outages. Ticketing notes: set SEV=high for billing triggers.

sam: handing off to me for follow-up and RCA. I'll keep the incident page updated and own postmortem.

alex: thx — documented mitigation steps and include exact pod IDs. leaving oncall to sam.

maya: next steps for post-incident: - revert the worker retry change if necessary - add connection leak detection metric - add circuit-breaker in client lib - add alert: idle_in_transaction > 30s count threshold.

sam: accepted handoff at 17:25 UTC. pd incident state: acknowledged -> monitoring. moving to post-incident.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 status updated: acknowledged -> resolved candidate.

alex: dropping a quick note for ops: we should consider lowering app db pool max to avoid exhausted PG maxconn in the future, add safe-fallback to replica for heavy ingest.

maya: filed follow-up ticket ENG-ops-871 in tracker with proposed remediation and owners.

sam: thanks all. will write the PM and link evaluation dashboards. closing thread once PM draft is up. :white_check_mark:
